title: Great Mosque of Cordoba
summary: The Great Mosque of Cordoba (Mezquita) was founded in the 8th century by Emir Abd al-Rahman I over the site of a Visigothic basilica, becoming the premier congregational mosque of Islamic Al-Andalus. Successively enlarged across three centuries under the Umayyad rulers, it was consecrated as a Catholic cathedral after the Christian conquest of 1236, later integrating a Renaissance cathedral nave within its expansive hypostyle prayer hall.

uncertainty.note: The Cabildo Catedral dates the foundational mosque of Abd al-Rahman I to 786-788 CE, while UNESCO dates construction broadly to the 8th century. Consecrated as a Christian cathedral in 1236, with major Renaissance additions between 1523 and 1599; standing today.
